newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arabs say Iran deploys missiles on islands.
newsitem.headline: Arabs say Iran deploys missiles on islands.

text.p: Eight Arab states said on Sunday Iran had deployed missiles on disputed Gulf islands and this was a direct threat to the Gulf Arab countries.

In a strongly worded statement after a two-day meeting in Cairo, the Damascus Declaration states -- Egypt, Syria and the six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) -- again demanded that Iran withdraw from the islands in favour of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), which also claims them.
The islands are Abu Musa, Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb, which lie close to Gulf shipping lanes and which have been at the centre of dispute between the two Gulf states since 1992.
Other Arab states regularly support the UAE's claim to the islands but the statement on Sunday broke new ground in saying Iran had deployed missiles on them.

Gulf states have previously complained that Iran has deployed surface-to-surface missiles in the region and the UAE Foreign Minister, Rashid Abdullah al-Nuaimi, said in November that it had deployed offensive weapons on the islands.

The statement on Sunday said: "The ministers...expressed their deep concern at Iran's deployment of surface-to-surface missiles in the Arabian Gulf, including its deployment of missiles on the UAE's three occupied islands, which exposes the GCC states and their vital installations to direct threat."
It comdemned what it said was Iranian persistence in imposing a fait accompli in the islands by force.
"The ministers...affirmed their absolute support for all peaceful measures and means taken by the UAE to recover sovereignty over these islands.
The members of the Gulf Cooperation Council are Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.
They signed the Damascus Declaration with Egypt and Syria after the Gulf War over Kuwait in 1991 and the eight foreign ministers meet twice a year to keep the alliance alive.
